G-IDS.note: verified now: foreign_key_check clean, entity_index consistent (132 ids)

G-DEC-STATUS.note: verified now (also DDL CHECK-enforced at write time)

G-REQ-SRC.note: verified now: NULL/whitespace-only provenance caught (the DDL CHECK misses whitespace-only)

audit_evidence.note: over each active AC's LATEST verdict (superseded verdicts are history, as acs-met reads them). Narrated = a graded verdict with no evidence, the graded party grading itself (C7). Ungraded = a Pending placeholder nobody has graded

G-REL.note: stored edges must satisfy RELATION_RULES. Retype a wrong edge in ONE entity_upsert batch: {retire: true} on the old triple + the correct relation. Use relates_to only when no typed relation fits and the link itself is real

requirements_unwired.note: non-retired requirements that miss a leg they owe. A leg is any link to a decision or ADR, a work item or slice, or a test (the G-TRACE reading). A requirement owes one leg. An Implemented requirement owes all three. `missing` names the legs per id. Wire derives_from, implements and tests in the session that creates the row. A scope-change link is not a leg. `waived` names an id the operator waived for `requirements-wired`. You never author a waiver on your own judgment. This rule never fails the gate
